families.title: Probabilistic programs: Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and further systems
families.intro: The programs of the Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and Geni papers, against Dice, Alea.jl and Roulette, and on the programs they take Geni, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Pluck, PITA, aspmc, Scallop, Storm, PRISM, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI and TensorInference.jl. tddlog runs its own encoding of a program's integers (binary, never one-hot) and is asked what the baseline answers: single marginals where the baseline gives single marginals, a distribution's values only where it computes them. Alea.jl's and Pluck's times leave out Julia's start-up and compilation, as Alea.jl's papers time it; the dashed lines add them to Alea.jl's, and Racket's start-up to Roulette's.

findings.title: The paper's samplers
paras: At the paper's precision the exact answer is closer to the model's than any sampler comes in its runs on GPA (1e-16, which tddlog computes in 41 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's MCMC with 10⁴ samples, comes to 2e-3 in 208 s); tug_of_war (5e-7, which tddlog computes in 0.8 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁷ samples, comes to 4e-5 in 52 s); conjugate_gaussians (5e-6, which tddlog computes in 1.8 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's rejection with 10⁶ samples, comes to 2e-4 in 71 s); zeroone_w1 (9e-5, which tddlog computes in 0.6 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁵ samples, comes to 2e-1 in 102 s); zeroone_w2 (5e-4, which tddlog computes in 2.5 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁵ samples, comes to 1e-1 in 102 s); coinBias (2e-7, which tddlog computes in 199 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁷ samples, comes to 1e-4 in 31 s); addFun_sum (4e-6, which tddlog computes in 1.2 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's rejection with 10⁶ samples, comes to 7e-4 in 7.3 s); clinicalTrial1 (5e-16, which tddlog computes in 2.9 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁶ samples, comes to 2e-3 in 311 s); clinicalTrial2 (7e-7, which tddlog computes in 0.04 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁷ samples, comes to 1e-4 in 87 s); and addFun_max (3e-7, which tddlog computes in 34 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's MCMC with 10⁷ samples, comes to 4e-4 in 68 s). On normal_mixture_theta, normal_mixture_mu1, normal_mixture_mu2, clickGraph, trueskill and conjugate_ex3 a sampler comes as close to the model as the exact answer at the paper's precision, sooner than the exact systems answer. Stan's HMC does not converge on altermu2, multimodal, zeroone_w1 and zeroone_w2: its error at its largest sample count stays above 1% of the answer.

findings.title: Answers
paras: tddlog's answers agree with the references everywhere, to 4e+5 relative against Alea.jl and exact references. ProbLog's d-DNNF is wrong on four bit-blasted circuits (clickGraph at 14 bits, by 0.016, pi at 12 bits, by 0.17, wmi_star at None bits, by 0.00022 and wmi_star at None bits, by 6.3e-05), which Ganak's exact count confirms. Dice prints 0 for every answer on 15 bit-blasted circuits, and Alea.jl's discretization is defective in the far tails of a normal, which moves the gene expression program's answer at Figure 2's precision from 1/2 to 0.333 with 5 genes and 0.482 with 20, where the artifact's own runs give 0.4999995 at every number of genes.

suites.title: The Dice paper's programs
suites.about: The programs and Bayesian networks of the Dice paper (Holtzen, Van den Broeck and Millstein, OOPSLA 2020), a network as one Dice program per queried variable, and its loop programs scaled up. tddlog runs them translated to ProbLog, Alea.jl translated to Julia, Roulette translated to Racket. 300 s a run (600 s on the loop programs). Geni, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Pluck, PITA, aspmc, Scallop, Storm, PRISM, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI and TensorInference.jl ran too, each on the programs it takes (its own paper's, the Dice programs, the ProbLog programs or the networks); a system's time is its process's, start-up included.

suites.title: Alea.jl's and noDice's programs
suites.about: Cao et al.'s integer arithmetic programs (UAI 2023), Pluck's sequence models (PLDI 2025) and noDice's purely probabilistic programs (OOPSLA 2026). Alea.jl runs an Alea.jl program itself; tddlog and Dice run the Boolean circuit Alea.jl builds for it, and Roulette that circuit's Dice program translated to Racket. The noDice programs are Dice programs, translated, and Roulette runs them translated to Racket. 600 s a run. Geni, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Pluck, PITA, aspmc, Scallop, Storm, PRISM, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI and TensorInference.jl ran too, each on the programs it takes (its own paper's, the Dice programs, the ProbLog programs or the networks); a system's time is its process's, start-up included.

suites.title: Bit-blasted programs
suites.about: The programs of the bit-blasting paper (Garg, Holtzen, Van den Broeck and Millstein, PLDI 2024) on ladders of precision. Alea.jl runs each program itself; tddlog runs the circuit Alea.jl builds for it, and Roulette the circuit's Dice program translated to Racket. 600 s a run. Geni, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Pluck, PITA, aspmc, Scallop, Storm, PRISM, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI and TensorInference.jl ran too, each on the programs it takes (its own paper's, the Dice programs, the ProbLog programs or the networks); a system's time is its process's, start-up included. 22 more instances of the ladders no system ran: each system had failed on a smaller size.

setup: Four lab machines: one with 16 physical cores and 251 GB of memory, for the Alea.jl and noDice programs; one with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, for the Dice paper's programs, Roulette's programs and the earlier run of Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs; one with 20 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, for the bit-blasted programs; and one with 36 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, for Geni's programs. A run is one job that holds its machine alone. Programs run as independent jobs in lanes, each pinned to one logical CPU on its own physical core, with the machine's memory split between the lanes. In a lane all systems run on an instance back to back, in an order rotated by instance and repetition, so that the systems share the lanes alike.

The release run, all of its parts at one version of tddlog, each part with all of its systems in the same lanes: the arithmetic, sequence and noDice programs (10 lanes, 25 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 251 GB of memory, 2026-10-29); the networks, the Dice paper's programs and the loop programs (8 lanes, 15 GB a process, three repetitions, 300 s for the networks and the Dice paper's programs and 600 s for the loop programs, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, 2026-10-22); Roulette's programs (4 lanes, 31 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, 2026-10-22); the bit-blasted programs for tddlog and Alea.jl (15 lanes, 33 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 20 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, 2026-10-29 and 30); and Geni's programs, with ProbLog's d-DNNF timed beside the others (16 lanes, 31 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 36 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, 2026-10-29). Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs come from an earlier run (5 lanes, 25 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, 2026-10-12) on the same circuits; neither those systems nor the circuits have changed since. Times compare within a run: on the bit-blasted programs the plots show tddlog and Alea.jl, and Dice's times are in the tables only. The plots of all programs put the runs together.

A program with a size runs from small to large, and a system that runs out of time or memory on one size is not run on the larger sizes of that program; the tables mark those `skipped`, and they count as failures. A failure of another kind skips nothing.
A time is the median of the repetitions, a failed repetition counted as longer than any time: of three repetitions, a system must answer in two.

For tddlog and Dice, the wall time of the process: parsing, compiling and answering every query. For Alea.jl, the time the program reports for building the model and computing its answers a second time in the same process, without Julia's compilation, as the papers time it; the process's wall time, with Julia's start-up, loading Alea.jl and compiling its methods, is the dashed line in the plots and the "process" column in the tables. For Roulette, the time the artifact's own `time` reports for building and querying the program; the dashed line adds Racket's start-up and loading.

The runs on the Alea.jl programs' circuits, Pluck's and noDice's programs, the runs on Geni's programs, the runs on the bit-blasted programs, the runs beside TensorInference.jl timed warm and the runs beside Scallop ran a build of 2026-10-28 (tididi ca759585, goatd e592d1e). The runs on Dice programs and LPADs ran a build of 2026-10-27 that reads Dice programs and LPADs itself (tididi 7eb08230, goatd e592d1e). The reruns of runs skipped without a failure on a smaller size ran a build of 2026-10-24 that adds a vtree search run to convergence (tididi ef11abfd, goatd e592d1e). The growth sizes ran a build of 2026-10-25 with twin contraction (tididi b9e5064e, goatd e592d1e) and a recursion over a successor relation grounded level by level, which lacks only the release's sparse route (tididi 9fc0a599). The runs on noDice's left-out programs ran a build of 2026-10-30 (tididi df7b84a3, goatd e592d1e). The runs on Bayesian and Markov networks ran a build of 2026-10-28 (tididi ca759585, goatd e592d1e). The runs beside Scallop ran a build of 2026-10-29 (tididi df7b84a3, goatd e592d1e). The runs beside TensorInference.jl timed warm ran a build of 2026-10-29 (tididi b5d9b21d, goatd e592d1e). Beside a cross job's systems, one run of tddlog on an instance where the rerun's was skipped ran that job's build, as of 2026-10-21 (tididi c7c0c5d6, goatd e592d1e). The release's main contains every solver change those builds have. Dice 1.0 (the binary of the `sholtzen/dice` image), with an unlimited stack. Alea.jl at revision cf5e5b8 on Julia 1.11.9 with CUDD 3.0.0 and Distributions.jl 0.25.131, one thread. Roulette from its PLDI 2025 artifact (revision 54d6185 of its repository) on Racket 8.16, the paper's Racket being 8.13 ([docs/baselines.md](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/docs/baselines.md), section 11). ProbLog 2.3.0 with `-k ddnnf`, timed on Geni's programs, a clique-tree solver and dynamic programs over the models' states as references, and for the bit-blasted circuits that Alea.jl does not answer, exact weighted model counts by Ganak in rational arithmetic.

Their versions are those of [docs/baselines.md](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/docs/baselines.md).

CmdStan 2.32.2 (the paper's 2.28.2 does not build both of the artifact's array syntaxes), WebPPL 0.9.15 on node 18, and Psi at revision ef8a9e5, each on the artifact's own program of the model, in the earlier run, three seeds. AQUA and GuBPI were installed but not timed ([docs/baselines.md](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/docs/baselines.md), section 10): the artifact's AQUA inputs crash it or answer other quantities on all but four programs, and GuBPI's repository has programs for three of the models and prints bounds rather than an answer. Mathematica, with which the paper simplified Psi's integrals, is not available. Some of the artifact's sampler programs encode another model than the HyBit program: Stan's and WebPPL's weekend, and WebPPL's clinicalTrial2 and zeroone. The table marks them "another model" and gives, in a note, the answer of the model each encodes, worked out by hand; it is the value their estimates settle on.
